headline: Normal 1Password app lock; broker healthy
summary: 1Password locked at 06:55:57 Eastern on October 22. The broker and keepalive remained healthy. No software repair is warranted. Unlocking 1Password and any required native consent remain Taylor’s actions.
cause: The bounded timestamped parser found a genuine lock event at 2026-10-22T10:55:57.866+00:00, matching saved keepalive state. No evidence supports a broker crash, stale watchdog or parser fault. The reason for the app lock is not established. Successful account calls at 06:49 Eastern predated the lock and do not prove current authorization.
resolution: No implementation changes, installation, restart or additional authorization wake were warranted or performed. Lock suppression is operating as intended. README.md links this verified incident and its authorization limits. No candidate fix was required.
verification: parser-check.json confirms readable logs and matching timestamped lock state without retaining raw lines. deployed-hashes.json verifies worker/keepalive source and deployed hashes, running keepalive hash, build stamp and signature. baseline.json and final-status.json show broker PID/session 1213, /dev/ttys000 and keepalive PID 1214 preserved, with heartbeat advancing from 06:56:35 to 06:56:55 Eastern. Account statuses stayed unchanged while locked. python-tests.json and broker-tests.json record 44 passing isolated Python tests; node-tests.json records 37 passing tests. metadata-smoke.json records wrapper --version exit 0 with output discarded; authenticated checks were skipped while locked. chat-check.json verifies the exact title, dotfiles directory, Pinned section, strongest advertised supported model gpt-6-astra and high reasoning.
activation: Existing signed service remains running unchanged. Nothing is staged and no activation is needed. Unlock 1Password when access is needed and complete native consent if requested; recovery owns any authorization wake.
limitations: Current account authorization was not tested while locked. Version success establishes wrapper responsiveness, not vault authorization. The exact app-lock trigger and physical notification-click behavior were not tested. No Computer Use or live Claude tests were performed.
docs: Reviewed src/onepassword/README.md, src/onepassword/agent-contract.md and src/onepassword/autofixes/AGENTS.md. Updated README.md with the October 22 morning evidence and authorization limits. The shared contract and autofix guidance already cover normal app locks; no contract edit or sync was needed.
